**Test image observations:**
- Soybean leaves with numerous small, scattered reddish-brown spots/pustules densely distributed across the leaf surface
- Spots are tiny, rust-colored, with some coalescing into larger patches
- Leaves show yellowing/bronzing with progression from individual dots to larger affected areas
- Field-level infection visible on multiple plants

**Analysis:**
The pattern of countless small, reddish-brown scattered spots densely covering soybean leaves is highly characteristic of **Soybean rust** (*Phakopsora pachyrhizi*). The rust-colored pustules (uredinia), the density of lesions, and the bronzing/yellowing of leaves all match. The reference collage for Soybean rust confirms this pattern — the microscopic view shows similar small brown pustule clusters, and the field-level images show similar bronzing with dense spotting.

This is distinct from Septoria brown spot (which has larger, more irregular angular lesions) and Cercospora (which tends to have larger, more defined circular lesions with lighter centers).
